thread.title: Apple: Bernstein Slashes iPhone Estimates But Urges Calm

author: Tiernan Ray
title: Apple: Bernstein Slashes iPhone Estimates But Urges Calm
text:
Although plenty of rumors are continuing to predict a deflation of Apple’s ( AAPL ) iPhone sales in the current quarter, Toni Sacconaghi of Bernstein today reminds investors the stock can continue to work based on rising sales prices, even if actual unit sales come in lower this year.
On a segment on CNBC a short while ago, with host Scott Wapner , Sacconaghi said it’s “hard to say” how much of the current quarter is factored into the stock at this point. But in today’s report, he makes the case investors should relax about the erosion of iPhone estimates.
Sacconaghi, who warned last week the quarter will probably come in weaker than expected when Apple offers its forecast this Thursday , after the closing bell, today formally cuts his numbers for iPhone. He now sees 53 million units for the quarter, below what he deems consensus for 62 million units.
And for the full fiscal year ending in September, he slashes his estimate to 220 million units from 247 million units previously estimated. The means almost no growth from last fiscal year — just 1.3% relative to 2017’s 216.76 million units.
Hence, the question of his report: “ Can the stock work if iPhone units don’t growth in 2018? "
Sacconaghi thinks the stock can, indeed, work, given the company may have net income in 2019 of “well over $14."
His estimate for this year is cut to $11.80 from $11.87.
But Sacconaghi emphasizes tax rate changes — perhaps as low as 14% going forward — and rising average selling prices — as things that can boost earnings in 2019 beyond the $13.06 he’s currently modeling:
We model (perhaps conservatively) 23M iPhone X units in FQ1 and 16M iPhone X units in FQ2, resulting in ASPs of $797 and $798, respectively. These ASPs are higher than consensus, and we believe it is difficult to get to consensus ASP in FQ1 of $751, unless iPhone X units are significantly lower. Furthermore, we believe currency could be a modest help to ASPs, although the impact is unclear given Apple's currency hedges. And lower our tax rate. Our research on tax reform suggests that Apple's normalized tax rate could be as low as ~14% on an ongoing basis.2 That said, we conservatively model an 18% tax rate in FQ2 18 onward. We also caution that FQ1 could contain a modest one-time tax charge from tax reform.3 FY19 EPS. We are also introducing a FY 19 EPS forecast of $13.06, driven by what we believe are relatively conservative assumptions. With incremental aggressive buybacks, FY 19 EPS could plausibly be $14 +. We assume: flat iPhone unit growth (which points to a continued elongation in iPhone replacement cycles); iPhone ASPs that decline 2% YoY (which may be conservative if the iPhone X+ gets a price increase, and other SKUs gain 3D sensing); a tax rate of 18% for the full year; services growth of 12%; overall margins flattish (pushed up by services, pressured by iPhone); and no buybacks beyond Apple recent historical repurchase rates. Importantly we note that every incremental $25B in incremental buybacks would push our EPS up by $0.46 […] EPS could be well over $14 if Apple chose to re-purchase significant amounts of its shares with its repatriated cash.
